title: 180223 CST 2a
description: Interview with Lt. Col. Richard Mohammadi, Commander 103rd Civil Support Team (CST) out of Alaska, and other members of the 14th CST from Connecticut that are participating in the Arctic Eagle 18 Exercise.  The mission they’ve been tasked with in this video is to identify a substance in the port that could be of radiological nature from a notional satellite that has crash landed. Arctic Eagle 18 is a statewide exercise involving national, state and local agencies designed to provide opportunities for participants to conduct sustained operations in arctic conditions. The goals of Arctic Eagle 18 are for participating forces to operate in a joint, interagency, and intergovernmental and multinational environment; assess ability to conduct sustained operations in arctic conditions, and integrate new and emerging capabilities.

transcript.text: Okay. All right, my name is Lieutenant Colonel Richard K.
Mohammed. I am the commander of the 103rd CST, which is the civil support team for
the State of Alaska. The 103rd currently is augmented by the 14th CST
out of Connecticut. They're here to help us out with the Arctic Eagle exercise.
Today, our mission is to investigate the chemical release of a substance on the
port and we're here in our efforts to identify that substance.
What are some of the steps that you go through?
The steps that we go through normally is that we make an IC link up and from that
link up we get the information that we need in order to respond to the situation
in the what's called the hot zone, which is basically the area closest to the
release. The most dangerous area around the chemical that we are trying to
identify. So what we do is in our process we set up our decon line and see behind
me and what we do is make sure that our individuals are briefed before they go
downrange and then they understand what it is that they're looking for. We take a
whole array of instrumentation down there in order to make sure that we have
every contingency covered. Once we find what we're looking for, we try to identify
it to specifically say this is either X or Y and basically if we can mitigate
that right then and there we will do so. However, the mitigation process will be
up to the IC in future efforts with a contractor to come out and clean it up.
It's like a setup here to decontaminate a personnel that you may find and it
gets handed in the zone, right? Yes, the CST is not equipped to deal with a
mass decontamination for other personnel. So it's called a technical decon line
which basically is for the CST personnel and the first responders that may go
downrange with us. And the reason that is we just do not have the resources
necessary to do a mass decontamination.
Actually, it's a little fold today. How does that work with the D-I?
It makes it a little bit more tricky but it doesn't inhibit us in any way.
Anything special you've learned or you've kind of prepared for being this
cold weather environment is exercise. The best thing that we learned is to make
sure that we have a lot of warming, we have a warming trailer and that we got
some warm food for the individuals. Just on a personal note, what's the best part of
your job? The best part of my job is getting my team together to do this job
and it's a great sense of satisfaction when we're able to help the IC and
mitigate any issues downrange and increase public safety.
I just thought of this to your mind. Can you tell me about how you integrate with the civil authorities here?
What way are you going to use?
So when we do deploy, we are under the incident commander. We report directly to
him and our directions come from him. Even though we are military units, we do
not come into this location to take over or to tell the IC what to do.
It's the other way around. We come here in support of the IC. We basically become
one of his assets for us to deploy.
This brings certain capability that we don't have.
That's correct. Yes. They don't have it has not capability here so whenever the need arises,
they can give us a call and we can be here as soon as we can get down to the
location.
